NKJV.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said:
NKJV.2: “Who is this who darkens counsel By words without knowledge?
NKJV.3: Now prepare yourself like a man; I will question you, and you shall answer Me.
NKJV.4: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell Me, if you have understanding.
NKJV.5: Who determined its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched the line upon it?
NKJV.6: To what were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,
NKJV.7: When the morning stars sang together, And all the sons of God shouted for joy?
NKJV.8: “Or who shut in the sea with doors, When it burst forth and issued from the womb;
NKJV.9: When I made the clouds its garment, And thick darkness its swaddling band;
NKJV.10: When I fixed My limit for it, And set bars and doors;
NKJV.11: When I said, ‘This far you may come, but no farther, And here your proud waves must stop!’
NKJV.12: “Have you commanded the morning since your days began, And caused the dawn to know its place,
NKJV.13: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked be shaken out of it?
NKJV.14: It takes on form like clay under a seal, And stands out like a garment.
NKJV.15: From the wicked their light is withheld, And the upraised arm is broken.
NKJV.16: “Have you entered the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in search of the depths?
NKJV.17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the doors of the shadow of death?
NKJV.18: Have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell Me, if you know all this.
NKJV.19: “Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place,
NKJV.20: That you may take it to its territory, That you may know the paths to its home?
NKJV.21: Do you know it, because you were born then, Or because the number of your days is great?
NKJV.22: “Have you entered the treasury of snow, Or have you seen the treasury of hail,
NKJV.23: Which I have reserved for the time of trouble, For the day of battle and war?
NKJV.24: By what way is light diffused, Or the east wind scattered over the earth?
NKJV.25: “Who has divided a channel for the overflowing water, Or a path for the thunderbolt,
NKJV.26: To cause it to rain on a land where there is no one, A wilderness in which there is no man;
NKJV.27: To satisfy the desolate waste, And cause to spring forth the growth of tender grass?
NKJV.28: Has the rain a father? Or who has begotten the drops of dew?
NKJV.29: From whose womb comes the ice? And the frost of heaven, who gives it birth?
NKJV.30: The waters harden like stone, And the surface of the deep is frozen.
NKJV.31: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, Or loose the belt of Orion?
NKJV.32: Can you bring out Mazzaroth in its season? Or can you guide the Great Bear with its cubs?
NKJV.33: Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?
NKJV.34: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That an abundance of water may cover you?
NKJV.35: Can you send out lightnings, that they may go, And say to you, ‘Here we are!’?
NKJV.36: Who has put wisdom in the mind? Or who has given understanding to the heart?
NKJV.37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of heaven,
NKJV.38: When the dust hardens in clumps, And the clods cling together?
NKJV.39: “Can  you hunt the prey for the lion, Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
NKJV.40: When they crouch in their dens, Or lurk in their lairs to lie in wait?
NKJV.41: Who provides food for the raven, When its young ones cry to God, And wander about for lack of food?

ESV.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said:
ESV.2: “Who is this that darkens counsel by words without knowledge?
ESV.3: Dress for action  like a man; I will question you, and you make it known to me.
ESV.4: “Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding.
ESV.5: Who determined its measurements — surely you know! Or who stretched the line upon it?
ESV.6: On what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
ESV.7: when the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
ESV.8: “Or who shut in the sea with doors when it burst out from the womb,
ESV.9: when I made clouds its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
ESV.10: and prescribed limits for it and set bars and doors,
ESV.11: and said, ‘Thus far shall you come, and no farther, and here shall your proud waves be stayed’?
ESV.12: “Have you commanded the morning since your days began, and caused the dawn to know its place,
ESV.13: that it might take hold of the skirts of the earth, and the wicked be shaken out of it?
ESV.14: It is changed like clay under the seal, and its features stand out like a garment.
ESV.15: From the wicked their light is withheld, and their uplifted arm is broken.
ESV.16: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep?
ESV.17: Have the gates of death been revealed to you, or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
ESV.18: Have you comprehended the expanse of the earth? Declare, if you know all this.
ESV.19: “Where is the way to the dwelling of light, and where is the place of darkness,
ESV.20: that you may take it to its territory and that you may discern the paths to its home?
ESV.21: You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
ESV.22: “Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
ESV.23: which I have reserved for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
ESV.24: What is the way to the place where the light is distributed, or where the east wind is scattered upon the earth?
ESV.25: “Who has cleft a channel for the torrents of rain and a way for the thunderbolt,
ESV.26: to bring rain on a land where no man is, on the desert in which there is no man,
ESV.27: to satisfy the waste and desolate land, and to make the ground sprout with grass?
ESV.28: “Has the rain a father, or who has begotten the drops of dew?
ESV.29: From whose womb did the ice come forth, and who has given birth to the frost of heaven?
ESV.30: The waters become hard like stone, and the face of the deep is frozen.
ESV.31: “Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loose the cords of Orion?
ESV.32: Can you lead forth the Mazzaroth  in their season, or can you guide the Bear with its children?
ESV.33: Do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you establish their rule on the earth?
ESV.34: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, that a flood of waters may cover you?

ESV.36: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts  or given understanding to the mind?
ESV.37: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can tilt the waterskins of the heavens,
ESV.38: when the dust runs into a mass and the clods stick fast together?
ESV.39: “Can you hunt the prey for the lion, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
ESV.40: when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in their thicket?
ESV.41: Who provides for the raven its prey, when its young ones cry to God for help, and wander about for lack of food?

NASB.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said,
NASB.2: 'Who is this that darkens counsel By words without knowledge?
NASB.3: 'Now gird up your loins like a man, And I will ask you, and you instruct Me!
NASB.4: 'Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell [Me], if you have understanding,
NASB.5: Who set its measurements? Since you know. Or who stretched the line on it?
NASB.6: 'On what were its bases sunk? Or who laid its cornerstone,
NASB.7: When the morning stars sang together And all the sons of God shouted for joy?
NASB.8: 'Or [who] enclosed the sea with doors When, bursting forth, it went out from the womb;
NASB.9: When I made a cloud its garment And thick darkness its swaddling band,
NASB.10: And I placed boundaries on it And set a bolt and doors,
NASB.11: And I said, 'Thus far you shall come, but no farther; And here shall your proud waves stop '?
NASB.12: 'Have you ever in your life commanded the morning, [And] caused the dawn to know its place,
NASB.13: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, And the wicked be shaken out of it?
NASB.14: 'It is changed like clay [under] the seal; And they stand forth like a garment.
NASB.15: 'From the wicked their light is withheld, And the uplifted arm is broken.
NASB.16: 'Have you entered into the springs of the sea Or walked in the recesses of the deep?
NASB.17: 'Have the gates of death been revealed to you, Or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
NASB.18: 'Have you understood the expanse of the earth? Tell [Me], if you know all this.
NASB.19: 'Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And darkness, where is its place,
NASB.20: That you may take it to its territory And that you may discern the paths to its home?
NASB.21: 'You know, for you were born then, And the number of your days is great!
NASB.22: 'Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, Or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
NASB.23: Which I have reserved for the time of distress, For the day of war and battle?
NASB.24: 'Where is the way that the light is divided, [Or] the east wind scattered on the earth?
NASB.25: 'Who has cleft a channel for the flood, Or a way for the thunderbolt,
NASB.26: To bring rain on a land without people, [On] a desert without a man in it,
NASB.27: To satisfy the waste and desolate land And to make the seeds of grass to sprout?
NASB.28: 'Has the rain a father? Or who has begotten the drops of dew?
NASB.29: 'From whose womb has come the ice? And the frost of heaven, who has given it birth?
NASB.30: 'Water becomes hard like stone, And the surface of the deep is imprisoned.
NASB.31: 'Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, Or loose the cords of Orion?
NASB.32: 'Can you lead forth a constellation in its season, And guide the Bear with her satellites?
NASB.33: 'Do you know the ordinances of the heavens, Or fix their rule over the earth?
NASB.34: 'Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, So that an abundance of water will cover you?
NASB.35: 'Can you send forth lightnings that they may go And say to you, 'Here we are'?
NASB.36: 'Who has put wisdom in the innermost being Or given understanding to the mind?
NASB.37: 'Who can count the clouds by wisdom, Or tip the water jars of the heavens,
NASB.38: When the dust hardens into a mass And the clods stick together?
NASB.39: 'Can you hunt the prey for the lion, Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
NASB.40: When they crouch in [their] dens [And] lie in wait in [their] lair?
NASB.41: 'Who prepares for the raven its nourishment When its young cry to God And wander about without food?

AMP.1: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind and said,
AMP.2:
"Who is this that darkens counsel [questioning my authority and wisdom]
By words without knowledge?
AMP.3:
"Now gird up your loins like a man,
And I will ask you, and you instruct Me!
AMP.4:
"Where were you when I laid the foundation of the earth?
Tell Me, if you know and have understanding.
AMP.5:
"Who determined the measurements [of the earth], if you know?
Or who stretched the [measuring] line on it?
AMP.6:
"On what were its foundations fastened?
Or who laid its cornerstone,
AMP.7:
When the morning stars sang together
And all the sons of God (angels) shouted for joy?
AMP.8:
"Or who enclosed the sea with doors
When it burst forth and went out of the womb;
AMP.9:
When I made the clouds its garment
And thick darkness its swaddling band,
AMP.10:
And marked for it My [appointed] boundary
And set bars and doors [defining the shorelines],
AMP.11:
And said, 'This far you shall come, but no farther;
And here your proud waves shall stop'?
AMP.12:
"Since your days began, have you ever commanded the morning,
And caused the dawn to know its place,
AMP.13:
So that light may take hold of the corners of the earth
And shake the wickedness out of it?
AMP.14:
"The earth is changed like clay into which a seal is pressed;
And the things [of the earth] stand out like a [multi-colored] garment.
AMP.15:
"Their light is withheld from the wicked,
And the uplifted arm is broken.
AMP.16:
"Have you entered and explored the springs of the sea
Or [have you] walked in the recesses of the deep?
AMP.17:
"Have the gates of death been revealed to you,
Or have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
AMP.18:
"Have you understood the expanse of the earth?
Tell Me, if you know all this.
AMP.19:
"Where is the way where light dwells?
And as for darkness, where is its place,
AMP.20:
That you may take it to its territory
And that you may know the paths to its house?
AMP.21:
"You [must] know, since you were born then,
And because you are so extremely old!
AMP.22:
"Have you entered the storehouses of the snow,
Or have you seen the storehouses of the hail,
AMP.23:
Which I have reserved for the time of trouble,
For the day of battle and war?
AMP.24:
"Where is the way that the light is distributed,
Or the east wind scattered over the earth?
AMP.25:
"Who has prepared a channel for the torrents of rain and for the flood,
Or a path for the thunderbolt,
AMP.26:
To bring rain on the uninhabited land,
And on the desert where no man lives,
AMP.27:
To satisfy the barren and desolate ground
And to make the seeds of grass to sprout?
AMP.28:
"Has the rain a father?
Or who has begotten the drops of dew?
AMP.29:
"Out of whose womb has come the ice?
And the frost of heaven, who has given it birth?
AMP.30:
"Water becomes like stone [and hides itself],
And the surface of the deep is frozen and imprisoned.
AMP.31:
"Can you bind the chains of [the cluster of stars called] Pleiades,
Or loose the cords of [the constellation] Orion?
AMP.32:
"Can you lead forth a constellation in its season,
And guide [the stars of] the Bear with her sons?
AMP.33:
"Do you know the ordinances of the heavens,
Or [can you] establish their rule over the earth?
AMP.34:
"Can you lift up your voice to the clouds,
So that an abundance of water will cover you?
AMP.35:
"Can you send forth lightnings that they may go
And say to you, 'Here we are'?
AMP.36:
"Who has put wisdom in the innermost being [of man, or in the layers of clouds]
Or given understanding to the mind [of man, or to the heavenly display]?
AMP.37:
"Who can count the clouds by [earthly] wisdom,
Or pour out the water jars of the heavens,
AMP.38:
When the dust hardens into a mass
And the clods stick together [because of the heat]?
AMP.39:
"Can you [Job] hunt the prey for the lion,
Or satisfy the appetite of the young lions
AMP.40:
When they crouch in their dens
And lie in wait in their lair?
AMP.41:
"Who provides prey for the raven
When its young cry to God
And wander about without food?

NLT.1: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:
NLT.2:
“Who is this that questions my wisdom
with such ignorant words?
NLT.3:
Brace yourself like a man,
because I have some questions for you,
and you must answer them.
NLT.4:
“Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?
Tell me, if you know so much.
NLT.5:
Who determined its dimensions
and stretched out the surveying line?
NLT.6:
What supports its foundations,
and who laid its cornerstone
NLT.7:
as the morning stars sang together
and all the angels shouted for joy?
NLT.8:
“Who kept the sea inside its boundaries
as it burst from the womb,
NLT.9:
and as I clothed it with clouds
and wrapped it in thick darkness?
NLT.10:
For I locked it behind barred gates,
limiting its shores.
NLT.11:
I said, ‘This far and no farther will you come.
Here your proud waves must stop!’
NLT.12:
“Have you ever commanded the morning to appear
and caused the dawn to rise in the east?
NLT.13:
Have you made daylight spread to the ends of the earth,
to bring an end to the night’s wickedness?
NLT.14:
As the light approaches,
the earth takes shape like clay pressed beneath a seal;
it is robed in brilliant colors.
NLT.15:
The light disturbs the wicked
and stops the arm that is raised in violence.
NLT.16:
“Have you explored the springs from which the seas come?
Have you explored their depths?
NLT.17:
Do you know where the gates of death are located?

WEB.7: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
WEB.8: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke out of the womb,
WEB.9: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,
WEB.10: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,
WEB.11: and said, ‘Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed?’
WEB.12: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place;
WEB.13: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?
WEB.14: It is changed as clay under the seal, and presented as a garment.
WEB.15: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.
WEB.16: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

WEB.18: Have you comprehended the earth in its width? Declare, if you know it all.
WEB.19: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,

WEB.29: Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?
WEB.30: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.
WEB.31: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?

WEB.39: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
WEB.40: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?

MSG.1: And now, finally, God answered Job from the eye of a violent storm. He said:
MSG.2:
"Why do you confuse the issue?
Why do you talk without knowing what you're talking about?
MSG.3:
Pull yourself together, Job!
Up on your feet! Stand tall!
I have some questions for you,
and I want some straight answers.
MSG.4:
Where were you when I created the earth?
Tell me, since you know so much!
MSG.5:
Who decided on its size? Certainly you'll know that!
Who came up with the blueprints and measurements?
MSG.6:
How was its foundation poured,
and who set the cornerstone,
MSG.7:
While the morning stars sang in chorus
and all the angels shouted praise?
MSG.8:
And who took charge of the ocean
when it gushed forth like a baby from the womb?
MSG.9:
That was me! I wrapped it in soft clouds,
and tucked it in safely at night.
MSG.10:
Then I made a playpen for it,
a strong playpen so it couldn't run loose,
MSG.11:
And said, 'Stay here, this is your place.
Your wild tantrums are confined to this place.'
MSG.12:
"And have you ever ordered Morning, 'Get up!'
told Dawn, 'Get to work!'
MSG.13:
So you could seize Earth like a blanket
and shake out the wicked like cockroaches?
MSG.14:
As the sun brings everything to light,
brings out all the colors and shapes,
MSG.15:
The cover of darkness is snatched from the wicked—
they're caught in the very act!
MSG.16:
"Have you ever gotten to the true bottom of things,
explored the labyrinthine caves of deep ocean?
MSG.17:
Do you know the first thing about death?
Do you have one clue regarding death's dark mysteries?
MSG.18:
And do you have any idea how large this earth is?
Speak up if you have even the beginning of an answer.
MSG.19:
"Do you know where Light comes from
and where Darkness lives
MSG.20:
So you can take them by the hand
and lead them home when they get lost?
MSG.21:
Why, of course you know that.
You've known them all your life,
grown up in the same neighborhood with them!
MSG.22:
"Have you ever traveled to where snow is made,
seen the vault where hail is stockpiled,
MSG.23:
The arsenals of hail and snow that I keep in readiness
for times of trouble and battle and war?
MSG.24:
Can you find your way to where lightning is launched,
or to the place from which the wind blows?
MSG.25:
Who do you suppose carves canyons
for the downpours of rain, and charts
the route of thunderstorms
MSG.26:
That bring water to unvisited fields,
deserts no one ever lays eyes on,
MSG.27:
Drenching the useless wastelands
so they're carpeted with wildflowers and grass?
MSG.28: And who do you think is the father of rain and dew,
MSG.29: the mother of ice and frost?
MSG.30:
You don't for a minute imagine
these marvels of weather just happen, do you?
MSG.31:
"Can you catch the eye of the beautiful Pleiades sisters,
or distract Orion from his hunt?
MSG.32:
Can you get Venus to look your way,
or get the Great Bear and her cubs to come out and play?
MSG.33:
Do you know the first thing about the sky's constellations
and how they affect things on Earth?
MSG.34:
"Can you get the attention of the clouds,
and commission a shower of rain?
MSG.35:
Can you take charge of the lightning bolts
and have them report to you for orders?
MSG.36:
"Who do you think gave weather-wisdom to the ibis,
and storm-savvy to the rooster?
MSG.37:
Does anyone know enough to number all the clouds
or tip over the rain barrels of heaven
MSG.38:
When the earth is cracked and dry,
the ground baked hard as a brick?
MSG.39:
"Can you teach the lioness to stalk her prey
and satisfy the appetite of her cubs
MSG.40:
As they crouch in their den,
waiting hungrily in their cave?
MSG.41:
And who sets out food for the ravens
when their young cry to God,
fluttering about because they have no food?
